posts.angle: Why does my dog do that. Circling, kicking grass, whiskers. Save bait.

slides.title: Why does my dog *do that?*
slides.sub: 3 odd habits, explained. Save this one.

slides.title: Spinning before bed.
slides.body: Many dogs circle before they lie down. AKC says it may be an old habit from wild ancestors who pressed down grass to make a bed.

slides.title: Kicking the grass.
slides.body: It is not to hide the mess. AKC says it may leave a scent message for other dogs. Their paws have scent glands.

slides.title: Those whiskers.
slides.body: They are sensors. AKC says whiskers can feel air move, which may tell a dog something is close before they touch it.

slides.title: Knowing dogs is our *job.*
slides.body: We watch how each dog plays and rests. Tell us about yours.

posts.caption:
Why does my dog do that?

1. Spinning before bed. It may be an old habit from wild ancestors who pressed down grass to make a bed.
2. Kicking the grass. It may leave a scent message. Dogs have scent glands in their paws.
3. Whiskers. They can feel air move, which may warn a dog that something is close.

Save this for the next time your dog does something odd.
